20.stem: 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ps: Life is full of possibilities. If we, like gardeners, provide a suitable environment and let children grow at their own pace, they will spontaneously explore the world, developing curiosity, creativity, and independence. Such children love life, dare to challenge, and possess initiative. But if we, like carpenters, always try to “shape” children into our ideal image, they will gradually lose autonomy, becoming accustomed to following others’ instructions. Such children quickly lose their sense of direction as they grow, because they are used to being arranged for, rather than actively choosing their path. As parents, our role should be that of gardeners, providing sunlight, rain, and fertile soil, allowing children to grow naturally at their own pace. It should not be that of carpenters, trying to carve out a “perfect” piece according to our will. The core of education starts with understanding life and helping children find their own “map” to find their direction in a complex world.

21.stem: 밑줄 친 a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3점]
ps: To see how borrowing and lending changes a person’s worldview, consider what the rate of interest does to people’s perception of time. Imagine you are lending to somebody at an interest rate of 10 percent per year for five years. This rate tells us that the money lent has a cost that reflects the risk of you not being repaid and the opportunity cost of not spending that money yourself. The longer the term of the loan, the higher the chance you won’t be paid back because it is further into the future — which by definition is unknowable — and the longer you will have to wait before spending the money yourself. In order to make this worthwhile for the lender, money has to have a price — a cost to the borrower and income to the lender. This price factors in the value of time. To put it another way, a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
opts: ① Lenders and borrowers benefit from each other.

④ Borrowing money involves the risk of damaging one’s credit.
⑤ Money you have now is more valuable than the same amount later.

ps: Social and environmental responsibility has become an increasingly important ethical consideration for content creators. As global awareness of social, environmental, and sustainability issues grows, many content creators are being called upon to consider the broader impact of their work. This includes addressing topics such as climate change, social justice, and ethical consumerism in their content. Content creators have a platform that can influence their audience’s attitudes and behaviors, and they have a responsibility to use that platform for positive change. For example, promoting environmentally sustainable products or supporting causes related to equality and justice can help raise awareness and drive meaningful social impact. Ethical content creators not only focus on promoting their products or services but also consider the values and causes they support, ensuring that their content aligns with their social and environmental principles.

23.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ps: Research on cephalopod neurobiology suggests that an octopus possesses roughly five hundred million neurons. What makes this system unusual is where many of those neurons are located. More than half are distributed throughout the arms rather than concentrated entirely in the central brain. Each arm contains networks of nerve cells capable of controlling complex movements and responding to sensory input locally. This means that many actions do not require detailed instructions from the brain itself. Instead, the arms function as highly capable extensions of the nervous system that interact with the environment directly. The suckers lining each arm play an important role in this process. These structures provide strong grip but also detect chemical signals on surfaces they contact. Marine biologists studying octopus behavior have shown that this allows the animal to gather chemical information through touch. In practical terms, an octopus can effectively taste what it touches.
opts: ① characteristics of an environment that suits an octopus
② function of the octopus’s central brain in controlling its arms
③ benefit of an octopus relying more on vision than touch for survival

ps: Consistent though he may be, some of Aristotle’s ideas meet us today as strange. He had no difficulty justifying slavery, for example, and in his era, philosophers enjoyed positions of high privilege and influence. It serves us to remember that every great thinker is of her own time and speaks to a particular audience, and certainly Aristotle is no exception. Human flourishing as he understood it probably would not be nearly as inclusive as we would want it to be today. How he understood right and good is best taken to be an indicator of how the privileged elite of ancient Greek society tended to understand right and good. 재판은 대중 광장에서 집행되어서는 안 되며, 그것은 오늘날 가상의 차원, 즉 소셜 네트워크로 전환된다.
민주적인 법치 국가에서, 재판하고 정의를 실현하기에 적절한 장소는 법정이며 대중의 압박에 영향을 받지 않는 방식이어야 한다.

ps: Human development is now increasingly understood as an ongoing, flexible, and evolving process rather than a fixed sequence of stages. In earlier views, development was believed to occur mainly during childhood, with adulthood seen as a period of stability and old age as a phase of decline. 34.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
ps: Social media has altered business, politics, and friendships, making going viral a household term. The global financial industry links every bank and countless households in every country, making us vulnerable to human error taking place on the other side of the world. As Columbia University strategy professor Rita McGrath explains, years ago most of our institutions were separate and thereby buffered from the effects of errors outside their walls. That is no longer the case. The digitization of massive amounts of information has continued to grow enormously as the cost of computing power has decreased. The development of smart systems that communicate autonomously gave rise to an infinite variety of potential breakdowns. This interdependence is a breeding ground for complex failure. As Rita puts it, when “things that used to be kept separate bump up against each other, it becomes far more difficult to predict what’s going to happen next.” Information technology creates new vulnerabilities because ______________________________.
opts: ① complex issues involving smart systems are oversimplified
② vast amounts of online information destroy social hierarchy
③ digitization widens the information gap between institutions
④ interconnectedness instantly spreads the impact of small failures
⑤ digital networks fall like dominoes due to increasing computing costs

35.stem: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
ps: Scientific developments and technologies in medical practice have brought us enormous progress in the treatment and prevention of infectious diseases. ①The discovery of penicillin in 1928 by Alexander Fleming, for which he later received the Nobel Prize, was one of the biggest breakthroughs in the battle against infectious diseases. ②Edward Jenner discovered around 1796 that humans were protected against the deadly smallpox virus after exposure to the cowpox virus, which is harmless to humans. ③A human’s average life expectancy has increased, but relying too much on medicine damages our body system. ④Vaccines developed in laboratories have contributed enormously to the reduction of the burden of bacterial and viral diseases and have even led to the elimination of poxvirus. ⑤For other infectious diseases (for example cholera and malaria), control and hygiene management measures have reduced their burden, while for others treatment therapies turned viral diseases that were deadly into chronic manageable diseases.

37.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
ps: Reappraisal — changing the way one thinks about emotional situations — might present a particularly effective avenue to regulating emotions because it transforms emotions at their root.

(A) This example illustrates how reappraisal might powerfully transform short-term emotional responses. When repeated over time, these short-term emotional consequences of reappraisal might accumulate to shape people’s psychological health. Thereby, reappraisal might be a key to resilience.

(B) Take, for example, someone who is going through a divorce. This is often an adverse event, and yet, it can be construed in different ways. One might view it as an overpowering loss that will mark one’s family for life. Alternatively, one might see it as something that is painful but that might lead to positive outcomes in the long run, such as improved relationships.

(C) As a result of these different construals, one might feel different emotions. The first construal may bring intense sadness and anger. The second construal might also bring sadness and anger but perhaps at lower levels. Crucially, it might also bring some positive emotions, such as hope, strength, or gratitude.

ps: We can’t utilize the same “one size fits all” rule for everyone because we use water for so many diverse things.

When we say that water is “clean,” we don’t just mean that it looks like a glass of water. ( ① ) Water quality is about following a certain set of criteria, or “benchmarks.” ( ② ) These guidelines inform us exactly how much physical, chemical, or biological stuff can be in the water. ( ③ ) These rules ensure the water is safe for anything we want to do with it, whether that’s drinking it at home, watering crops on a farm, or running it through a huge industrial boiler. ( ④ ) For instance, the water that cools down a huge power plant generator doesn’t need to be as clean as the water you drink from the kitchen tap. ps: Dolphins’ brains have evolved specialized areas dedicated to echolocation, allowing them to process acoustic information more quickly and with less energy. One key adaptation is the structure of the dolphin’s auditory pathway. The signals from the ears are rapidly transmitted to the auditory cortex, the brain region responsible for processing sound. However, unlike many other mammals, dolphins have a highly specialized auditory cortex with distinct areas dedicated to processing different aspects of echolocation signals. Some areas may be responsible for analyzing the timing of echoes, while others focus on the frequency content or the intensity of the sound. This specialization allows the dolphin’s brain to process echo information in parallel, rather than sequentially. Imagine a factory assembly line, where different workers are responsible for different tasks. By dividing the work among specialized areas, the brain can process information much faster and more efficiently. This parallel processing reduces the cognitive load associated with echolocation, allowing dolphins to react quickly to changes in their environment.

41~42.tr: [해석] 무료함이 적절하게 다뤄지지 않는다면 우울, 낙담, 그리고 짜증과 같은 해로운 감정들을 발생시킬 수 있다는 것을 인식하는 것은 중요하다. 우리가 행복해지는 유일한 방법이 재미있는 활동들을 찾는 것에 의해서만이라고 믿으면, 그때 우리는 그러한 활동들에 의존하게 되고, 부정적인 생각들과 감정들이 생긴다. ‘아무것도 안 하는 시간은 악마의 작업장이다’라는 것은 자신의 손에 너무 많은 시간을 가진 사람들이 그 시간을 문제를 일으키는 생각들과 행동으로 채울 수 있다는 것을 암시한다고 일컬어진다. 균형점은 그것을 아무것도 안 하는 시간, 낭비된 시간, 또는 무료함으로 보는 것이 아니라, 오히려 자기 개선, 자기 발견, 그리고 긍정적인 성찰 시간을 위한 완벽한 시간으로 보는 것이다.
ko: 무료함이 적절하게 다뤄지지 않는다면 우울, 낙담, 그리고 짜증과 같은 해로운 감정들을 발생시킬 수 있다는 것을 인식하는 것은 중요하다.
우리가 행복해지는 유일한 방법이 재미있는 활동들을 찾는 것에 의해서만이라고 믿으면, 그때 우리는 그러한 활동들에 의존하게 되고, 부정적인 생각들과 감정들이 생긴다.
‘아무것도 안 하는 시간은 악마의 작업장이다’라는 것은 자신의 손에 너무 많은 시간을 가진 사람들이 그 시간을 문제를 일으키는 생각들과 행동으로 채울 수 있다는 것을 암시한다고 일컬어진다.
균형점은 그것을 아무것도 안 하는 시간, 낭비된 시간, 또는 무료함으로 보는 것이 아니라, 오히려 자기 개선, 자기 발견, 그리고 긍정적인 성찰 시간을 위한 완벽한 시간으로 보는 것이다.
곰곰이 생각해 보면 우리가 무료할 수 있어서 정말 얼마나 행운인가?
무료함은 위험이 존재하는 곳에서는 존재하지 않는데, 왜냐하면 그것이 단지 안전지대 안에서의 탐닉 활동이기 때문이다.
무료함은 안전하고 할 일이 없는 상황들에서 전형적으로 나타나는 사치로 인식될 수 있으며, 환경을 인식하고 이해할 기회를 제공한다.
위험한 상황들에서, 무료함이라는 사치는 손에 넣을 수 없다.
따라서, 심오한 자기 성찰을 위해 아무것도 안 하는 순간들을 활용하는 것은 가장 중요하다.
그것은 표현하기 전에 경청하고, 관찰하고, 그리고 인식할 기회를 의미한다.
무료함을 비생산적이라고 여기기보다, 그것은 개인적 발달과 건설적인 사유를 위한 기회로 여겨져야 한다.
